messages:
Maya: Quick design q — the new 'rainbow' metric palette in dark mode is making chart lines hard to follow. See screenshot in thread. Thoughts?

Alex: Totally. Red/green pairs disappear for deuteranopia, and the legend labels fall into background. Contrast on legend text is ~3.2:1.

Devon: +1. Also the saturated hues on #0B0F14 (console bg) feel harsh. I'd prefer muted tones with stronger luminance deltas.

Rachel: Proposal: switch to a colorblind-safe qualitative palette (e.g., ColorBrewer/Okabe-Ito) and increase label contrast to >= 4.5:1. Also add shape/patterns for line styles on accessible mode.

Maya: Ok — can you paste suggested hexes? Also how does this affect the token heatmap? It uses a continuous gradient.

Devon: Suggested swaps (try these on dark bg):
```
--chart-1: #88C0D0;
--chart-2: #EBCB8B;
--chart-3: #D08770;
--chart-4: #A3BE8C;
--chart-5: #B48EAD;
```
These are desaturated and have clearer luminance separation.

Alex: For continuous heatmaps, avoid full rainbow. Use a sequential perceptually-uniform scale (Viridis / Inferno) with a dark midpoint. Also expose a 'color-blind' toggle in Console > Settings so we can respect user prefs.

Rachel: Accessibility nit: legend icons need larger hit targets and a hover tooltip. Also use `aria-label` on SVG paths; keyboard focus styles should be visible (not just outline: none).

Maya: Copy tweak: instead of 'Colorblind mode' label should be 'Color accessibility: high contrast & patterns'. Longer but clearer.

DesignBot: Automated check — legend text contrast 3.2:1 (FAIL); suggested contrast target 4.8:1 using #E6EEF6 on #0B0F14.

Devon: I'll mock a variant with those colors + patterned lines for high-contrast mode and post PNGs.

Alex: If possible, run a quick AB with the deployment banner chart — check task completion time & misread rates in usability tests.

Maya: Sweet. @Devon pls drop mocks here by EOD. Thanks :thumbsup:
